audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read 'Skill' on all seven rows while the content layer read Swain on all seven — the page answered 'who wins Level 1' two different ways. Separately, the packet itself flags the chart as contradicting the data: Diana wins 57.08% over 1468 games yet the chart gives Swain 7/7.
audit.why: I fixed only the cross-layer disagreement, by moving the full layer onto the content layer's existing verdict rather than inventing a new one. I did not resolve the 7/7-vs-57.08% contradiction: I cannot tell from the kits which rows should flip, and inventing a power shift is worse than a stale row. Raised in questionsForUser.
audit.corrected: All seven phases[N].side set to Swain to match win[N], with every why rewritten to a kit-grounded reason for that verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: Demonic Ascension was described only as 'his drain mode' with no number, and one bullet offered a 'fifteen-second invitation' after he wastes it. It is a flat 120s.
audit.why: Riot's text: the form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions — you cannot wait it out inside 650, you have to break contact. The real punish window is 120 seconds long, not fifteen.
audit.corrected: Flat 120s, 650 radius, no natural expiry while he is draining a champion; Nevermove 12s at rank 1; Death's Hand 7s down to 3s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content named a 'Torment/Nevermove root chain' — Torment is not in Swain's kit — and called Ravenous Flock a 'passive DoT'. It is a heal plus permanent max-health gain off Soul Fragments.
audit.why: Riot's text for the passive. Nevermove is the one root, and critically it roots on the RETURN, not the throw, then lets him pull rooted champions closer — the exact reason a markless Lunar Rush (14s at rank 5) into him ends inside Death's Hand.
audit.corrected: Named Nevermove's root-and-pull correctly and replaced the DoT claim with Ravenous Flock's healing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was mentioned only as a vague 'add anti-heal early', and the resistance point was absent.
audit.why: missingInteractions: needs-antiheal and resistances-invalidated — his sustain, not his burst, is what beats you, so stacking raw MR does not answer it.
audit.corrected: Itemization now says rush anti-heal and states that MR alone will not answer the drain.

audit.why: 57.08% over 1468 games is the figure on the page; I left it alone, but it is the number that makes the 7/7 chart suspect.

notes: CHART, IMPORTANT: the packet's own defect list says this chart contradicts the data — Diana wins 57.08% over 1468 games while the chart gives Swain 7 of 7 stages. I did NOT resolve that, because nothing in the kits tells me which rows should flip and inventing a power shift is the one thing the brief forbids. What I did fix is the separate cross-layer defect: the full layer said 'Skill' on all seven rows while the content layer said 'Swain' on all seven, so the page rendered two different answers to every row. I moved the full layer onto the content layer's existing verdict (no new verdict invented) and rewrote all seven whys to kit-grounded reasons. No win[N] edit is proposed because win[N] already holds the target value on disk. 'Torment' was a genuine fabricated ability name in spikes[0].text and is removed. Not asserted, since the kits do not answer it: whether Nevermove's root can be cleansed or QSS'd before the pull resolves, and whether Diana's Moonfall pull can drag Swain out of his own Demonic Ascension radius.
